Estevao has refused to address reports linking him with a move to Paris Saint-Germain but says he has received ‘a lot of motivation’ during the international break having struggled for playing time at Chelsea this season.

The 19-year-old has started just one game in the Premier League this season and delivered an impressive performance in Chelsea’s 2-0 win at home to Manchester United on October 31.

However, Estevao was back on the bench for Chelsea’s 1-0 defeat to Sunderland on November 8, although he was brought on as a half-time substitute during the loss at the Stadium of Light.

Xabi Alonso praised Estevao’s response after he was left as an unused substitute during Chelsea’s penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup last month and has insisted that the Brazilian winger ‘will have his moment’ this season.

However, reports have claimed that Estevao has been unhappy with his lack of playing time under Alonso and is considering his future at Chelsea.

Estevao started in both of Brazil’s friendlies during the international break and delivered a lively display during the 7-0 win over Singapore on Tuesday as he scored a goal and registered two assists.

‘I’m very happy to have received the minutes in the friendlies,’ Estevao told ESPN Brasil after his national side’s win at the National Stadium in Singapore.

‘I thank Ancelotti for his confidence because every player wants to play and at Chelsea I’ve had few minutes, but coming here and knowing that the manager trusts me gives me a lot of motivation.

‘We think about ourselves, what we can do better… whether the stadium will be full or not, we think about doing our part so that we can improve.

Chelsea’s next Premier League fixture is at home to Leeds United on Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino insists that he wants to be involved in "all the main decisions" at Manchester United.
  • Pochettino has been appointed as "head coach" of Man Utd, a role he held at both Tottenham and Chelsea, rather than be known as the first-team manager.
  • The main difference between the two job titles is often considered level of input or control of decisions beyond tactics and team selection.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino insists that he wants to be involved in "all the main decisions" at Manchester United.

Pochettino has been appointed as "head coach" of Man Utd, a role he held at both Tottenham and Chelsea, rather than be known as the first-team manager.

The main difference between the two job titles is often considered level of input or control of decisions beyond tactics and team selection.

Mikel Arteta has most notably been promoted from head coach to manager during his seven years at Arsenal, and is widely understood to have a say in almost every key aspect of the club's running.

Pochettino is seemingly not asking for such a level of input, but as the January transfer window approached he has made it clear that he wants a greater say on his players in the future.

"I was in all my career a coach, head coach, manager," he told reporters on Friday. "It does not change too much.

"I know as head coach I am the guy who tomorrow will decide the squad for Sunday, pick the 11, make the changes.

"I know in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that affect the squad. At the end of the day, Manchester United is a football club.".

Pochettino kicks off his Man Utd reign at Liverpool on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool youngster Trey Nyoni has picked out Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard as the ‘toughest opponent’ he has faced at the start of his career.

Odegaard has returned to his sparkling best this season, starting all ten of Arsenal’s opening matches in the Premier League with the reigning champions sitting five points clear at the summit.

Having managed just one goal across the Gunners’ title-winning campaign last term, the 27-year-old appears to have rediscovered his scoring boots, finding the net on five occasions in all competitions this term.

It was Odegaard’s 72nd-minute strike that proved the difference before the international break, when Mikel Arteta’s men were made to work for their victory at home to newly promoted Hull City.

The Norway international will no doubt be desperate to pick up where he left off when the north London giants return to top-flight against at Newcastle on Saturday evening.

Nyoni has himself enjoyed an impressive start to the season at Liverpool and locked horns with Odegaard when the pair did battle at Anfield at the start of the month.

And while Nyoni was taken off before the hour-mark on Merseyside, it’s clear Odegaard left a major impression on the 19-year-old in the 58 minutes his opposite number was on the pitch.

Asked to name the ‘toughest’ player he has come up against, Nyoni told The Inside Scoop, ‘For me personally, I would say Odegaard,’ as he looked back on that afternoon.

‘The way he plays, it’s very busy, moving around and always looking for an option.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

According to recent reports, ‘It’s not easy as a midfielder. I think when you play against someone who is constantly moving, you know in the back of your mind that he could be here, but the next minute he’s there.’.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

When asked if Odegaard perhaps doesn’t get the credit he deserves, Nyoni replied: ‘Yeah, I think the game is evolving and I think nowadays people look at No.10s and automatically think that if they’re not getting goals and assists, they’re not good.

‘For example, in our team we’ve got Flo [Wirtz]. I think Flo does a lot of stuff that people don’t really see.

‘I think what he brings to the team benefits the team. Just because he’s not scoring or assisting, doesn’t mean he’s not effective.

‘Nowadays, the idea that if a player isn’t getting goals or assists, they’re useless, but every player has their own role in the team.

‘Odegaard and people like Flo, if they’re not getting goals and assists, people that don’t watch the game automatically think they haven’t played well but that’s not how football works.’.

In the aftermath of Arsenal’s nervy win over Hull, club legend Paul Merson noted Odegaard had been ‘like a new signing’ for Arteta this season.

According to recent reports, ‘He’s been outstanding. He’s the only one really that moves it rapidly,’ Merson said of Odegaard on Sky Sports.

‘He moves it rapidly, he moves, he gets into positions. I just thought too many players took too many touches and they slowed it down and gave Hull half a chance.

‘I think he’s been outstanding this season, he’s like a new signing for them and he’s been the man so far.

Sources indicate that ‘Not great but just a good result for Arsenal. But again, he was one of the stars of the show.’.

Manchester United could push for Villarreal full-back Alex Freeman in January, a player Mauricio Pochettino has tipped to become ‘one of the best in the world’ in his position.

Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick’s successor last week and will arrive in Manchester today ahead of his first game in charge away to Liverpool this weekend.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager will be backed in the January transfer window with a striker and a full-back thought to be priorities.

Recent findings suggest that USA international Folarin Balogun is reportedly a target United are considering to bolster their options up top. The Daily Telegraph report another name has been discussed in Freeman, a player Pochettino is a huge admirer of.

The right-back joined Villarreal in January 2026, thriving under head coach Inigo Perez and emerging as an crucial member of the first-team. Having started out as a winger, he has established himself at right-back, having also played on the left.

Pochettino recognised the 22-year-old’s qualities while at the helm of the US men’s national team, giving him his senior debut and starting him in four of their five matches at the World Cup.

‘He is so humble, he has an amazing profile, he always listens,’ Pochettino said after Freeman scored in the USA’s World Cup win over Australia in June.

According to recent reports, ‘You really enjoy being with him, coaching him, and [he] is an amazing player. For me, [he has potential] to be one of the best players at his position in the world.’.

United have also been linked with another USA international in Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson with former Premier League star Darren Bent believing he and teammate Calvin Bassey would be ‘very good additions’ to United’s backline.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ashley Young reckons it is time for Manchester United to move on from Bruno Fernandes and feels there is a Premier League star who should be signed to replace him.

Fernandes has consistently been the Red Devils’ best player since joining from Sporting in January 2020.

However, at 32 years old and with latest manager Mauricio Pochettino arriving this week, doubts over whether Fernandes will remain the focal point of the team are being raised.

The United captain is into the final few months of his contract and has reportedly rejected two offers of a new deal.

The club has the option to extend his current contract by another month, which would prevent Fernandes leaving on a free transfer in the summer, but he could still be sold in 2027 if that option is taken up.

Former Red Devils man Young reckons it is time to move on from Fernandes and thinks the man to replace him is Nottingham Forest and England midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White.

The former Wolves star turns 27 in January and Young feels now is the time for Manchester United to make him their main man, replacing Fernandes.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He’s been unbelievable for the club, the standout performer,’ Young said of Fernandes on Overlap Daily. ‘But there’s been so much that’s come about. He’s turned down another contract, we’re hearing.

‘You want to build around a player. He’s 33 next year. Age is nothing but a number, but he’s not in his peak. I wouldn’t say past it, but he’s getting older now.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘For me, I would go and sign Morgan Gibbs-White. I’m just throwing that name out there. But you’re thinking a number 10 and you want to build a team around a player.

In a recent development, ‘He’s young, he’s hungry, he’s just got in the England squad. I think he’s got the capabilities to go and play for – no disrespect to Nottingham Forest – a bigger club. And I think he’s someone that Manchester United need, in his peak years.

‘I think he’s shown more than enough at Nottingham Forest to be able to go and say I can play for a bigger club like Manchester United and take the weight of that.’.

As much as signing fresh players will be on the agenda for the new Manchester United manager, getting rid of unwanted squad members may be the bigger test.

Gary Neville feels there needs to be a significant cull over the next few transfer windows, with some massive names ideally being axed at the end of the season.

Sources indicate that ‘If you look through it now I’d say Martinez would go, [Matthijs] De Ligt would go, [Noussair] Mazraoui would go, [Mason] Mount would go, first wave next summer. [Marcus] Rashford if you can, and [Joshua] Zirkzee,’ the former full-back mentioned on Stick to United.

‘And then the year after you’d be looking at [Luke] Shaw, [Harry] Maguire, [Diogo] Dalot, Bruno [Fernandes], that’s your second wave and maybe then you’ve made your mind up on [Carlos] Baleba and [Andrey] Santos.

‘But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.’.

  • Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has confirmed a quadruple injury boost for his side ahead of Sunday's blockbuster Premier League battle with Manchester United at Anfield.
  • The Reds have the honour of hosting Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils, in which they will endeavour to improve on a paltry record of just one win from five home matches in the 2026-27 top flight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 14:06.

Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has confirmed a quadruple injury boost for his side ahead of Sunday's blockbuster Premier League battle with Manchester United at Anfield.

The Reds have the honour of hosting Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge of the Red Devils, in which they will endeavour to improve on a paltry record of just one win from five home matches in the 2026-27 top flight.

Liverpool maintained their excellent away form by beating Crystal Palace 3-1 before the international break, but Dominik Szoboszlai emerged as an injury worry following the Selhurst Park success.

The midfielder nevertheless joined up with Hungary for the November international break and played the full 90 in both of their Nations League games against Georgia and Northern Ireland, supplying two assists against the former.

Szoboszlai was managing a knee problem during his time with the Magyars, but speaking to the media on Friday, Iraola affirmed that the 26-year-old will be fine for Sunday's main event.

"He's in a good place, he's playing normally, he was not even strapped today so he's fine yes," Iraola responded when asked if Szoboszlai was still being carefully looked after.

As well as confirming Szoboszlai's availability, Iraola delivered positive updates on the Dutch trio of Ryan Gravenberch, Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk.

The latter withdrew from the Netherlands squad for the November window due to an unspecified fitness problem, while Gravenberch and Frimpong were both absent from the win over Palace.

Frimpong sustained a hamstring injury against Brentford in October and has missed Liverpool's last six games in all competitions, while Gravenberch has been dealing with a minor heal fracture.

However, all three are in line to feature against old rivals Man United, as Iraola added: "If everything goes to plan they should be available for the game.

"Gravenberch, it's a matter of pain, he's managing but he's been training the last two days. Jeremie is recovering the same. We've introduced him with the rest of the group, and Virgil is fine to go.".

Should all of Szoboszlai, Van Dijk, Gravenberch and Frimpong make the cut, Liverpool's only remaining concerns are the long-term trio of Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitike.

The latter is still a while away from making a full recovery from an Achilles injury, but Leoni and Bradley have returned to team training as they close in on returns from serious knee injuries.

Recent findings suggest that however, Iraola confirmed that neither defender will be in the squad on Sunday, adding: "The international break was the best moment to introduce them slowly, they've started doing things with the team. They are still not available, but it's very good news and I hope they can play in some weeks.".

Liverpool sit fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points from their opening 10 games, but they have won just two of their last nine matches against Man Utd.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

The supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Recent findings suggest that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

It was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

It has been revealed that equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Recent findings suggest that carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

It has been revealed that in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

Industry observers note that “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager mentioned. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

It does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

According to recent reports, marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

It has been revealed that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

United fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Industry observers note that speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick mentioned: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

In a recent development, “But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. Industry observers note that when asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

“We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

“We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

Balde has not started a single match this term, managing just 124 minutes of action in five appearances off the bench. The situation has prompted fresh speculation over his future with United still in desperate need of another option at left-back.

Upcoming United boss Mauricio Pochettino will be backed in January with a new striker and a left-back to be targeted.

Mundo Deportivo report Balde’s agent Jorge Mendes arrived in Barcelona on Tuesday with his client’s future one of the topics on the agenda.

Balde is unhappy with his role at the Camp Nou and while there are no offers on the table as of yet, that could soon change.

Bayern Munich were also credited with interest in the summer but the report adds Balde is eager to test himself in the Premier League.

Barcelona are remarked to value Balde at €40million (£33m) and are reportedly prioritising a permanent sale, but a loan deal with an option to buy could also be considered.

Chelsea have been fined £150,000 as an FA punishment for offensive chanting during last season’s FA Cup game against Charlton was upheld on appeal.

The charges relate to chanting in the 56th minute of January’s 5-1 win at Charlton, which was Liam Rosenior’s first match in charge of the club.

Chelsea admitted the charge but then appealed against the punishment to an independent body, which upheld the initial punishment.

An FA statement on Friday afternoon read: “Chelsea FC has been sanctioned for crowd misconduct in relation to an FA Cup fixture against Charlton Athletic FC.

“It was alleged that around the 56th minute Chelsea FC failed to ensure its spectators and/or supporters (and anyone purporting to be supporters or followers) did not behave in an improper, offensive, abusive or insulting way with either an express or implied reference to religion or belief.

“Chelsea FC admitted the charge and an independent Regulatory Commission imposed an action initiative, £150,000 fine and warning as to future conduct following a hearing.”.

Recent findings suggest that the statement continued: “The club subsequently appealed against these sanctions. The appeal was dismissed by an independent Appeal Board and the orders of the Regulatory Commission stand.”.

Chelsea confirmed the verdict in a statement of their own on Friday, adding: “We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

Recent findings suggest that “Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.

“Chelsea takes a zero-tolerance approach towards discriminatory behaviour in whatever form it takes. We will always take steps to identify those responsible and take appropriate action where necessary.

“We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future.

“We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.”.

#37579. Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2114 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

Industry observers note that the club’s new managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

According to recent reports, ‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but quickly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

Industry observers note that salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

Industry observers note that they are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

‘You can’t be yourself,’ claims Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

Recent findings suggest that like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

According to recent reports, grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady remarked that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

Intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

City have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

He utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

The format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

Industry observers note that ‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson says, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

‘You're having the same conversations again. It was like, "Hang on a minute. I've had this conversation before". The previous people knew about it. They have the footage from earlier seasons – so do your homework, like we all do with our jobs. It almost felt like a bit of a lack of respect at times.’.

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for an eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise cameras were rolling.

Former Sunderland boss Simon Grayson was unaware of their planned Netflix documentary and didn't grant the producers access to his inner sanctum.

According to recent reports, these are the challenges that Amazon face with United, somehow attempting to earn trust or forging relationships in a matter of months before they pack up and leave. The film crew will be seen as outsiders.

There is intrigue within the industry as to exactly how granular Amazon can go amid the United chaos and whether they use fly-on-the-wall cameras, as was the case with Arsenal (in 2021–22) and Tottenham (in 2019-20).

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for that eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise the cameras were rolling.

Unlike Mourinho, Pochettino – his predecessor, sacked in November 2019 – had banned them from his office. He was never keen on the idea of the documentary and hardly features in the series, his dismissal coming early in Episode One – a sign perhaps that the film-makers got little out of him.

It will be fascinating to see if they gain access to his inner sanctum at United.

The club have had to double their media commitments this season as a result of the streaming deal, although they have been reluctant to organise sitdown interviews with players, telling Amazon that they must establish their own rapport for those.

Sources indicate that some clubs have been known to give their content away for free, with Sky Sports taking two seasons of Mission to Burnley without paying. The driving force behind those moves is to promote brands. Under Alan Pace’s premiership, Burnley are staring at potential relegation to League One.

Vincent Kompany, then the Burnley manager, is understood to have been vexed at his portrayal as a hot-headed screamer. Brendan Rodgers cannot have been overly pleased with Being: Liverpool, which ended in public ridicule and comparisons to David Brent. Players at other clubs have confided that they hid from cameras.

‘You can’t be yourself, you never forget the cameras are there,’ says Grayson of his season alongside the makers of Sunderland 'Til I Die.

Salford's co-manager Anthony Johnson gives his players a dressing down in the BBC documentary.

It has been revealed that joey Barton, meanwhile, is still waiting for his moment – and may be for some time. Fleetwood Town commissioned their own team to chart his start in management and streaming giants Dazn purchased the rights.

Industry observers note that it was so close to being aired that Fleetwood held a premiere at Highbury Stadium for 100 supporters including the local mayor, only for one of Barton’s brushes with law enforcement in the intervening days to suspend the broadcast. Prolonged legal proceedings meant the idea was canned and Dazn’s licencing period expired.

It was later resurrected, focusing in part on then Fleetwood owner Andy Pilley’s fraud trial – a crew followed him into court on day one – but was then shelved when a guilty verdict was handed down. Cameras are following clubs up and down the EFL from Birmingham to Cambridge via Sheffield Wednesday.

Grayson, for his part, refused to share his drive home from training with the crew and now admits that the ultimately unfavourable edit may have been a result of him not giving the production company what they wanted.

It has been revealed that ‘I did a presentation with the players with a flip chart and everybody thought it was an hour before kick-off of a league game,’ he claims. ‘It was actually done at 11:30am before a pre-season game!

Recent findings suggest that 'That’s why I let them film it, because it was a pre-season game, and it had no real meaning. But they presented it in the doc as if it was before the first game of the season.

It has been revealed that 'Part of the severance when I was sacked was that I still needed to do some work for them. I did three different (choreographed) interviews in a London hotel with different shirts on after I’d been sacked, done as if they were filmed at the time.

‘People remarked, “You didn’t come across that passionate about the club when you were talking about it”. Well, why would you when you were filming in November after you’d already been sacked? We were talking about deadline day in one of them. I’d already done something on that in August.

According to recent reports, ‘I think they had sympathy with me, but also if they’d had more sympathy, they wouldn’t have even asked me to do it. I’ve spoken to managers since and they’ve gone, “F***ing hell, you did well to put up with that".'.

Grayson only ever watched four episodes back and has heard his successor, Chris Coleman, was also dealt a raw deal.

Fabian Delph leads a Manchester City inquest during an FA Cup defeat at Wigan - the only scene from the dressing room that made it into Amazon's documentary on the 2017-18 season.

Mauricio Pochettino banned cameras from his office in his final days at Tottenham. Will he do the same at Manchester United?

In a recent development, by his own admission, Johnson enjoyed the process more than Grayson did. One ex-Salford player claimed that nothing was really cut from the show other than a fight on a team-bonding night out. It was authentic, no-holds barred.

Until the end of Johnson and Morley, that is.

‘We won the league and we ended up getting sacked anyway,’ Johnson claims. ‘We went to meet Gary (Neville) and the board. We went upstairs in Hotel Football and a cameraman followed us. Obviously they knew what was going on. When we got to the room for the meeting, they wouldn't let the camera in.

‘I'm actually smiling thinking about it. The documentary followed me and Bern everywhere, eating food or whatever, and then when the day comes to sack us, they didn't want the camera in the room!

‘The conversation was fine in the room itself but I think the perception from the outside world looking in would've been: "What the f*** is that all about?”’.

Manchester United have identified three potential defensive signings for Mauricio Pochettino in the January transfer window, according to reports.

Pochettino arrived at United’s training ground on Wednesday afternoon to begin his stint as head coach following the decision to sack Michael Carrick last week.

United have faced criticism over their transfer activity in the summer as they spent £155 million on signing three midfielders in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.

Pochettino now arrives at Old Trafford short of options with striker Benjamin Sesko sidelined until next year with a shin injury, while Luke Shaw has missed United’s last seven fixtures.

According to Sky Sports, United are willing to bolster Pochettino’s squad in the January window and the club will consult the Argentine over any potential signings.

The report claims that Everton centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey are two players who United are considering for January.

United had two bids rejected for Branthwaite in 2024, including an offer of £50 million, and held talks with the defender’s representatives earlier this year.

The report adds that Fulham left-back Antonee Robinson is also one of United’s options and the 29-year-old has already played under Pochettino with the United States national team.

Elsewhere, reports in Spain claim that Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde is open to a move to United in the upcoming transfer window.

However, Balde has not started a game in La Liga or the Champions League this season and Barcelona remain open to selling the defender.

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 14:08.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed that Joao Pedro remains unavailable for Saturday's Premier League fixture against Leeds United.

However, despite suggesting that he was dealing with fitness issues while on international duty with Ecuador, Moises Caicedo has been declared fit.

The Blues return to action this weekend sitting in fifth place in the Premier League table, yet Alonso is under pressure to deliver after four defeats in 10 top-flight matches.

Pedro has been sidelined since the October 17 game at Everton with a thigh injury, and it remains unclear when he will return.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Alonso stated that two players had been passed fit, while three players in total are still ruled out.

When quizzed on Pedro, the Spaniard told reporters: "Not yet. He's not fit yet to train with the team.

According to recent reports, "He's not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling.".

Alonso went on to say that Maxence Lacroix, who suffered a hamstring injury versus Liverpool on October 28, was in a similar situation to Pedro, while Jorrel Hato remains out with a back problem.

Nevertheless, as well as Caicedo being passed fit, Josh Acheampong will be back in the squad after missing one Premier League game and two England Under-21 matches with a minor concern.

Meanwhile, Alonso has added that Reece James is still "some weeks away" from returning from a knee injury that required surgery.

However, despite not being back in contention this week, Alonso revealed that Jamie Gittens is training with the first-team squad after six weeks out with an ankle injury.

Moises Caicedo has revealed he asked to be substituted at half-time playing for Ecuador as Chelsea were handed a scare during the international break.

Ecuador played friendly matches against Costa Rica and Bolivia, picking up 2-0 victories in both games.

Caicedo played 84 minutes in Quito in what was Marcelo Gallardo’s first game in charge on Saturday, named in the starting XI again on Tuesday.

The former Brighton star was replaced halfway through that game, later revealing he was ‘not feeling well’ with Chelsea’s game against Leeds United on Saturday in his thoughts.

Recent findings suggest that ‘No, I didn’t feel very well, so I asked to come off instead, because I know I have another commitment with my club.,’ Caicedo told reporters. ‘So, I’ll try to get there as soon as possible and recover.’.

Caicedo missed Chelsea’s opening game of the season against Fulham, suffering a calf injury 14 minutes after coming off the bench in the following game against Brighton.

He was ruled out of the next three games but has started Chelsea’s last five in the Premier League.

He was also a doubt heading into the game against Sunderland before the international break.

During the international break, the 25-year-old opened up on his recent fitness complications.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘[I’m] a little tired, with some minor complications, but I’m here because it’s my national team and what matters most to me is being here; with my people, with my Ecuador,’ he remarked.

‘I’m making a big effort to be here, and I’m happy about that.’.

Caicedo is not expected to return to Chelsea training until Friday and will likely have just one session to prove his fitness ahead of the visit of Leeds on Saturday afternoon.

Chelsea return to action sat in fifth place in the English top flight.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that early and late H.
  • Sources indicate that establishing the environmental context of H.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka)2. Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil3, Sangiran4 and Ngandong2 (in Java) open woodland–grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus5, found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens, and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus.

Recent findings suggest that early and late H. erectus finds in East and Southeast Asia represent a key part of the hominin evolutionary history of the Asian region, with China sitting in an important location to understand the dispersal, interactions and adaptations of this species6,7,8. There is a rich fossil record for H. erectus in China in Yuanmou (1.7 million years ago)9,10,11, Gongwangling (1.6 million years ago)12, Zhoukoudian (780–400 ka)13, Nanjing (approximately 650 ka)14 and Hexian (410 ka)15 (Supplementary Information 1). However, most of these sites are located in north and central China, with reliably identified and dated H. erectus fossils being conspicuously rare in southern China, especially during the Middle Pleistocene. This makes it particularly challenging to establish their ecological preferences. Furthermore, evidence of younger H. erectus (less than 400 ka) is almost entirely absent from China. This temporal gap is particularly striking given that H. erectus persisted in Java until 117–108 ka at Ngandong2, raising fundamental questions about the species’ distribution, ecological adaptations and ultimate fate in mainland China.

Sources indicate that establishing the environmental context of H. erectus is essential for understanding the species’ ecological flexibility and adaptive capabilities. The youngest Javanese H. erectus at Ngandong2 persisted in woodland refugia as rainforests expanded across the region, raising questions about whether encroaching closed-canopy forests contributed to the species’ eventual extinction2,16. Yet, there have been very few stable isotope studies on H. erectus evidence, as the material is often limited by diagenetic alteration3. Recent work has debated whether non-H. sapiens Middle Pleistocene hominins possessed the adaptive capabilities to exploit tropical rainforest environments17,18. Studying the forested landscapes of tropical southern China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene19 thus provides a crucial test case for assessing H. erectus ecological adaptations. Furthermore, understanding mobility patterns through techniques such as strontium isotope analysis can reveal how these populations used their landscapes and how they connected with contemporaneous populations across broader regional scales20,21.

Sources indicate that since the Pleistocene, tropical forest and grassland environments in southern China have provided a critical biogeographical corridor for faunal dispersals between northern latitudes and insular Southeast Asia22,23,24. The karst landscapes and cave systems of the region have yielded abundant Pleistocene faunal assemblages, yet there is presently no clear evidence that H. erectus was part of the Stegodon–Ailuropoda fauna in this region6. This raises questions as to whether the absence of H. erectus in southern China, particularly during the late Middle Pleistocene, is a consequence of ecological constraints preventing H. erectus from exploiting southern China’s tropical forest environments18, representing an effective biogeographic barrier25, or results from other factors such as an imbalance in research intensity7, a reflection of real absence of the species in the region due to alternative dispersal routes through the Tibetan corridor6, the absence of secure dating data on many out-of-context teeth, the misidentification of fragmentary remains (particularly with morphologically similar Pongo teeth26), taphonomic and preservation biases in tropical environments18, lower population densities leading to reduced fossil representation27 or the occupation of an ecological niche that is not readily preserved in cave deposits18. Distinguishing between these scenarios requires well-dated, robustly identified hominin fossils with detailed environmental context—evidence that has been lacking.

To provide a temporal and environmental context for the eight H. erectus teeth6 from Baxian and Naxian caves in southern China (Fig. 1, Supplementary Information 2 and 3 and Extended Data Figs. 1–3), we used five independent dating techniques to constrain the sediments: post-infrared infrared-stimulated luminescence (pIR-IRSL) dating of feldspars, optically stimulated luminescence (OSL) dating of quartz (Supplementary Information 4), uranium-series (U-series) dating of fossil teeth (Supplementary Information 5), coupled U-series–electron spin resonance (US-ESR) dating of fossil teeth (Supplementary Information 6) and U-series dating of carbonate capping flowstones (Supplementary Information 7), all integrated through the use of two Bayesian age models—ChronoModel and OxCal (Supplementary Information 8). Environmental reconstruction was achieved through faunal analysis (Supplementary Information 3), bulk and sequential stable isotope analysis of faunal and H. erectus tooth enamel (Supplementary Information 9) and clumped isotope thermometry of cave sediments (Supplementary Information 10). Finally, we assessed individual mobility patterns through laser-ablation trace element mapping and strontium isotope analysis of hominin tooth enamel, integrated with a regional strontium isoscape constructed using random forest machine learning to identify potential source regions (Supplementary Information 11). These multiple lines of evidence, replicated across laboratories in China and Australia, provide, to our knowledge, the first comprehensive temporal, environmental and behavioural context for late H. erectus in southern China.

a, The locations of China (green region on the world inset), Beijing (black dot) and the Chongzuo study area located in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region province, southern China (black star). b, The location of Chongzuo city in relation to Nanning and Hanoi, illustrating the dense network of karst (tan topography) that comprises this landscape. The black dashed box marks the study region and the red square represents the cave locations. The location of the lower section of Red River valley in Vietnam (discussed in the text) is marked by a red dashed line. c, Location of the Naxian and Baxian caves (red stars) connected by a 15-km karst corridor near the meandering Zuojiang River and the city of Chongzuo. Scale bars, 100 km (b), 10 km (c). Maps adapted from ref. 19, CC BY 4.0.

According to recent reports, the Naxian and Baxian caves, located 15 km apart and situated 13 km to the northwest and 20 km to the north of Chongzuo City, respectively, are connected by a straight karst valley corridor (Fig. 1, Extended Data Fig. 1a,b,e,f and Supplementary Information 2). They are both horizontal caves at 226 and 218 m above sea level, positioned 5–7 m above the valley floor (Extended Data Fig. 2), with small fossil chambers at the rear of each cave (Fig. 2). The chambers contain remarkably similar dense, cemented, cataclastic breccias that have yielded a combined total of over 18,000 mammalian fossils, which were initially accumulated by porcupines28, including hominin remains (Supplementary Information 2). The fossil-bearing breccias (Extended Data Fig. 3) were capped by thick flowstone and underlain by younger mixed sediments (Extended Data Fig. 1d,h). This similarity suggests deposition under comparable environmental conditions.

It has been revealed that a, Cave initiative for Naxian cave, showing the locations of the test pits (T1–T3) and fossil chamber at the rear of the cave. b, Expanded illustration of test pits T1 and T2 and fossil chamber in a, showing the spatial relationship between the sampling locations. c, Cross-sectional stratigraphic profile of the fossil chamber and excavation pit T2, drawn from location A–A′ in a, showing the sampling locations in the breccia, flowstone and underlying mixed unit. d,Cave plan for Baxian cave, showing the location of the two fossil chambers at the rear of the cave and the location of the test pits (T1–T3). e, Cross-sectional stratigraphic profile of the fossil chamber and excavation pit T2 drawn from location B–B′ in d, showing the sampling locations that correspond to the legend. f, Enlarged fossil chamber, showing the spatial location of the sampling in pits T2 and T3 in d. g,h, Composite stratigraphy for Naxian (g) and Baxian (h) caves, showing the sampling locations within the flowstone, breccia and underlying sandy clay. At each location, the symbols refer to the dating techniques in the legend, and the sampling codes and results have been included. Scale bars, 5 m (a), 1 m (c,e), 10 m (d).

Of the resulting 45 radiometric ages from both caves (Extended Data Figs. 4–7), 43 were modelled and given similar modelled age estimates (OxCal: 312–161 ka; ChronoModel: 324–184 ka at 2σ uncertainties; Extended Data Fig. 8), but the ChronoModel results were used owing to their greater outlier robustness and more reliable lower age limit. These results indicate that the age of H. erectus fossil evidence lies between 324 and 184 ka for the Baxian caves, and between 319 and 241 ka for the Naxian caves. These error limits are overlapping and broadly contemporaneous, and indicate a 95% probability that H. erectus was in this area sometime between 324 and 184 ka (see Supplementary Information 4–8 for all dating tables, data and discussion of limitations, uncertainties and choice of model; Fig. 3). The overlapping age uncertainties for the caves of approximately 78,000 years suggest a contemporaneous or near-contemporaneous presence on this landscape. The modelled ages are consistent across all five dating techniques within their respective uncertainties, providing robust constraints on the timing of H. erectus presence in this region.

A large proportion of taxa from both sites fall within the dense-canopy forest zone, supporting the interpretation of closed-canopy rainforest environments. Scale bars, 50 km (c). Bax, Baxian; Nax, Naxian.

Industry observers note that the faunal assemblages from the Baxian and Naxian caves are taxonomically diverse and remarkably similar in composition (Supplementary Information 3 and Extended Data Fig. 3). Both assemblages include numerous taxa that have since become locally extinct, including Pongo, Elephas and rhinoceros Dicerorhinus, though most remain extant elsewhere in Asia. Notably, H. erectus, Stegodon and ‘Megalovis’ are globally extinct. Habitat preference analysis indicates that both assemblages are strongly dominated by forest-dwelling taxa (Supplementary Fig. 3), which is consistent with predominantly forested landscapes during the time of deposition.

The plant-equivalent stable carbon isotope values for the Baxian faunal teeth, after correction for species-specific diet-to-enamel enrichment factors based on body mass29 (Supplementary Information 9), range from −31.5 to −23.0‰ (average = −27.6 ± 1.87‰ (1σ)), while lower values observed at the Naxian cave range from −34.0 to −25.1‰ (average = −29.4 ± 2.45‰ (1σ)). Both assemblages yield values well below the dense-canopy forest threshold of −27.5‰ (ref. 28), with no evidence of C4 plant consumption or even C3–C4 intermediate signatures (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 9). These data indicate that the fauna at both sites derived their dietary carbon exclusively from C3 vegetation, with the frequency of canopy-related values exceeding those reported for equatorial African rainforest systems29 and being comparable to that documented for western Amazonian forests30,31,32. This pattern is particularly notable given that several of the taxa represented in the assemblages are known elsewhere to exploit mixed C3–C4 resources or to incorporate substantial C4-derived inputs into their diets in more open environments16.

Sources indicate that independent oxygen isotope (δ18O) and clumped isotope (Δ47) analyses further support these environmental reconstructions, indicating humid tropical conditions with higher precipitation and cooler temperatures than modern values in this region (Extended Data Fig. 9 and Supplementary Information 9 and 10).

Three H. erectus teeth from the Naxian cave (NX-B1, NX-B2 and NX-A1) show similarly low isotopic values, with carbon values ranging from −15.0 to −14.0‰, which fall at the boundary between dense-canopy forest and more open C3 vegetation. Although the dataset is limited (n = 3) and currently restricted to the Naxian locality, these values are fully consistent with those observed across the much larger faunal assemblage and fall within the range expected for consumers deriving their dietary carbon from closed-canopy C3 vegetation, demonstrating that these late H. erectus populations exploited tropical rainforest resources.

High-resolution trace element mapping on one H. erectus individual from the Baxian cave (PA1799) yielded 87Sr/86Sr ratios ranging from 0.7110 to 0.7220 (Supplementary Information 11 and Extended Data Fig. 10), while three H. erectus teeth sampled from the Naxian cave showed overlapping but distinct ranges. All four individuals indicate either movement between geologically distinct regions or consumption of resources from multiple locations during childhood (2–6 years), corresponding to the period of tooth formation.

Recent findings suggest that A regional strontium isoscape for southern China and northern Southeast Asia33 (Supplementary Information 11) reveals substantial spatial heterogeneity in predicted 87Sr/86Sr ratios, with the local Baxian–Naxian region characterized by relatively homogeneous values (0.710–0.715), reflecting the dominant Carboniferous–Permian limestone karst geology (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 10). More radiogenic signatures (0.717–0.723) occur to the west and northwest in mountainous areas underlain by Precambrian and Palaeozoic metamorphic rocks, while intermediate to more radiogenic values (0.715–0.720) characterize regions to the south, including the Red River valley of northern Vietnam.

Geographic assignment probability maps generated for three representative 87Sr/86Sr values observed in the human tooth profiles indicate that these H. erectus individuals may have moved between the local limestone karst regions and more distant areas during childhood, with the most radiogenic signatures potentially pointing towards areas as far afield as northern Vietnam, which connect southern China with mainland Southeast Asia (Figs. 1 and 3 and Extended Data Fig. 10).

Industry observers note that our results demonstrate that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka (Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 8), representing, to our knowledge, the youngest reliably dated occurrence of this species in China and the first with robust chronological constraints from southern China. The integration of multiple independent dating techniques combined with Bayesian age modelling provides unprecedented temporal resolution for late H. erectus in mainland Asia. These findings fundamentally alter our understanding of the species’ persistence and distribution in China, extending the documented record by more than 200,000 years beyond the previous youngest occurrences in Hexian and Nanjing14,15, and establishing southern China as a key region for late-surviving populations during the late Middle Pleistocene (for example, ref. 19).

Recent findings suggest that the temporal importance of this discovery extends beyond simply filling a chronological gap. The age uncertainty range of 324–184 ka places these H. erectus populations at some point within marine isotope stages 9 through 6, raising intriguing questions about potential contemporaneity or overlap with Homo longi (Denisovans) identified in Cobra cave (Laos)34, Baishiya cave (Tibetan Plateau)35, Harbin (northeast China)36,37,38 and the Penghu Channel off the western shore of Taiwan39. The temporal proximity of these various hominin populations across China during the late Middle Pleistocene suggests a more complex biogeographical landscape than previously recognized, with multiple hominin lineages potentially coexisting across different ecological zones and elevational gradients.

According to recent reports, moreover, the environmental context revealed by our multi-proxy analyses challenges prevailing assumptions about late H. erectus ecological constraints and mobility patterns. The combined evidence demonstrates unequivocally that these late H. erectus populations exploited closed-canopy tropical rainforest environments and may have conducted long-distance movement beyond the local karst terrain during childhood. The ecological implications of this rainforest use and mobility are profound. Archaeological evidence has so far suggested that H. sapiens was the only member of our genus to specialize in the regular exploitation of these environments18, as early as 150 ka in western Africa40,41. In Southeast Asia, recent isotopic observations of declines in C4 environments and expansion of rainforest in the Middle to early Late Pleistocene have been associated with the disappearance of non-H. sapiens hominin taxa42,43, seemingly unable to shift from mixed savannah–woodland habitats to these increasingly closed forests16,44. However, our data directly challenge this view by demonstrating that H. erectus was not ecologically excluded from rainforest environments (Fig. 3) and that long-distance mobility into these environments may have been a common behavioural pattern rather than exceptional behaviour by isolated individuals.

These findings contrast markedly with Early and Middle Pleistocene H. erectus occupations at Trinil3 and Sangiran in Java4 (Extended Data Fig. 9b). The youngest Javanese H. erectus at Ngandong2 persisted in relatively open woodland refugia2, leading to suggestions that expanding rainforests may have contributed to the species’ eventual extinction in Java2,16. Among early hominin-bearing sites in East and Southeast Asia (Extended Data Fig. 9b), the Naxian and Baxian cave results most closely resemble those from Lida Ajer, Sumatra (73–63 ka), an early H. sapiens site also characterized by closed-canopy rainforest45. This demonstrates that H. erectus was, at minimum, capable of persisting among rainforest fauna, even if such habitats did not represent its optimal ecological niche.

Areas in northern Vietnam, such as the Red River valley (Figs. 1 and 3), have long been recognized as a critical biogeographical corridor connecting the karst uplands of southern China with the lowlands of mainland Southeast Asia24. The limited strontium isotope evidence tentatively suggests that late H. erectus populations may have been utilizing similar corridors for seasonal movements, long-distance migrations or resource procurement. This large range (potentially around 250 km) through mostly enclosed environments challenges assumptions about the limited ranging behaviour of H. erectus and suggests behavioural sophistication in landscape use.

Our findings collectively demonstrate that late Middle Pleistocene H. erectus was present in southern China, surviving contemporaneously with H. longi and exhibiting considerable ecological and behavioural flexibility. Rather than being restricted to open savanna or woodland habitats, as traditionally assumed, these populations persisted in closed-canopy tropical rainforests while simultaneously engaging in potential long-distance mobility across diverse ecological and geological landscapes. This evidence challenges the characterization of H. erectus as a species unable to exploit complex tropical forest environments. Whether these adaptations were specific to the late-surviving populations in southern China alone remains to be seen, but further stable isotope work on other Middle Pleistocene sites is vital to address this question. However, the presence of morphologically and genetically confirmed H. erectus in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, combined with the environmental and suggested mobility evidence, is sufficient to necessitate a re-evaluation of the species’ adaptive capabilities, biogeographical range and ultimate fate in mainland Asia.

The caves were discovered using local knowledge and targeted reconnaissance hunting for breccia in the rear chambers. The locations of test pits within the caves were selected on the basis of these reconnaissance surveys. Excavation grids were based on the shape of cave passages and distribution of fossil-rich deposits. Jackhammers were used to break blocks of fossil breccia, and the fossils were extracted using geological hammers. Fine cleaning, identification and cataloguing were conducted in the laboratories at Shandong University and the Institute of Vertebrate Palaeontology and Palaeoanthropology (IVPP).

According to recent reports, the fossil-bearing breccia and associated sediments from the fossil chambers of both caves were sampled in situ under subdued red-light conditions (Fig. 2a,d) and were processed using standard sample purification procedures for quartz and feldspar separation including a 40% and 10% wash in hydrofluoric acid for 45 and 10 mins, respectively46. Single aliquots of 90–125 µm feldspar and 180–212 µm quartz or feldspar grains were processed in a Riso TL-DA-20 equipped with an automated DASH set-up, a dual-laser single-grain attachment47 and a blue- and ultraviolet-sensitive Electron Tube photo-multiplier tube (PDM9107Q-AP-TTL-03), using either a blue filter pack (Schott BG-39, 2 mm, and Corning 7-59, 4 mm) for feldspars or U340 filters (2 × Hoya U340, 3.5 mm) for quartz. Data were collected using Sequence Pro v.4.65 and analysed in Analyst v.4.57, DRAC v.1.3 and on spreadsheets designed in Microsoft Excel 365 v.2607. Feldspar equivalent doses were corrected according to the results of the anomalous fading tests (using a weighted mean fading rate of 2.0 ± 0.2% per decade)48, but no residual corrections were undertaken, and the equivalent doses for both feldspar and quartz were then run through either a central age model for the single-aliquot results or a minimum age model49 to identify the single-grain population that experienced the most bleaching before burial. All luminescence analysis was conducted at the ‘Traps’ luminescence dating facility at Macquarie University in Sydney, Australia.

Recent findings suggest that measurements of 238U, 235U, 232Th and 40K were estimated using Geiger–Muller multi-counter beta counting and thick-source alpha counting of dried and powdered sediment samples in the laboratory, combined with in situ gamma spectrometry in the field. The corresponding (dry) beta and gamma dose rates were obtained using the conversion factors in ref. 50 and the beta-dose attenuation factors in ref. 51. Cosmic-ray dose rates were estimated from previously published relationships52, making allowance for the sediment overburden at the sample locality (ranging from 3.99 to 0.20 m), the altitude (ranging from 2,000 to 176 m above sea level) and geomagnetic latitude and longitude of the sampling sites.

Seven H. erectus teeth from the Naxian (n = 6) and Baxian (n = 1) caves were analysed for U-series dating across two laboratories in China and Australia. U-series measurements were undertaken using a laser-ablation multi-collector inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometer (MC-ICP-MS) at the Geoarchaeology and Archaeometry Research Group (GARG), Southern Cross University, according to protocols in ref. 53 and in a Neptune MC-ICP-MS at the School of Geography Science, Nanjing Normal University according to refs. 54,55. Laser ablation (at Southern Cross University) was performed with a New Wave Research 213 nm laser, and thorium (230Th, 232Th) and uranium (234U, 235U, 238U) isotopes were measured on a Thermo Neptune XT MC-ICP-MS. Teeth were ablated using rasters of 5 min each and were measured with standards before and after. Uranium and thorium were separated using conventional anion-exchange chromatography at Nanjing, and the U–Th solution was then introduced into the MC-ICP-MS via a DSN-100 desolvation nebulizer system. Isotopic ratios were measured using a detector configuration that allows for the simultaneous measurement of U and Th isotopes56,57.

Industry observers note that one H. erectus tooth and one Pongo tooth from the Baxian cave (n = 2) were selected for coupled ESR and U-series dating at GARG, Southern Cross University. Enamel fragments from each tooth were separated using a hand-held diamond saw following the protocol developed in ref. 58. Fragments were then measured at room temperature on a Freiberg MS5000 ESR X-band spectrometer at a modulation amplitude of 0.1 mT, 10 scans, 2 mW power, 100 G sweep and 100 kHz modulation frequency. Each fragment was irradiated, following exponentially increasing irradiation times. Sediment elemental concentrations, external beta and gamma dose rate contributions, and water content were obtained from in situ measurements. The external beta-dose rates have been extrapolated from the U, Th and K contents measured on a portion of sediment sub-sample (approximately 8 g). The external gamma dose rates were determined in situ using a portable gamma spectrometer at each site. The equivalent doses were estimated using Matlab-based MCdose software v.2.0.

Separate sub-samples were hand-drilled from the fresh cross-section of the in situ capping flowstones from Naxian and Baxian caves and processed at the Radiogenic Isotope Facility, University of Queensland (n = 6), and six soda straws and one sample of secondary calcite cement were processed at the School of Geography Science, Nanjing Normal University (n = 7). The powdered sub-samples were subjected to chemical treatment and isotopic measurements by mass spectrometry56. U-series dating of the speleothem samples were conducted at the University of Queensland using a Nu Plasma MC-ICP-MS, and analytical procedures followed previous publications for MC-ICP-MS57,58,59. The 230Th/234U ages were calculated using Isoplot EX 3.75 (ref. 60) and half-lives of 75,690 years for 230Th and 245,250 years for 234U (ref. 61). U-series dating of the speleothem samples was carried out at Nanjing Normal University using a Neptune MC-ICP-MS. U-series ages were calculated using the half-lives of 75,584 years for 230Th and 245,620 years for 234U (ref. 62). Non-radiogenic 230Th was corrected using an assumed bulk-Earth atomic 230Th/232Th ratio of (4.4 ± 2.2) × 10−6 (refs. 54,55).

Sources indicate that two Bayesian modelling programs were used to analyse selected independent age estimates (n = 43) (Supplementary Information 8) and to evaluate the uncertainties associated with the combined dating techniques applied to both sites (Supplementary Tables 7–15): OxCal (v.4.4.4, available at https://c14.arch.ox.ac.uk/oxcal.html)63 and ChronoModel (v.3.2.7, https://chronomodel.com/)64. The analyses incorporated the probability distributions of individual ages, constraints imposed by stratigraphic relationships and the reported minimum or maximum nature of some of the individual age estimates. Each individual age was included as a Gaussian distribution (with mean and s.d. defined by the age estimate and their associated uncertainties), and the resulting age ranges for each phase of deposition were presented at 2σ. OxCal allows the identification of boundary ages between each layer to constrain the fossil layer and ChronoModel was applied to assess the extent to which identical or similar data could be obtained. Both modelling results have been presented for transparency.

In a recent development, three H. erectus specimens from the Naxian cave, as well as 47 faunal teeth from the Baxian cave and 38 from the Naxian cave (n = 41 in total), were taxonomically identified and prepared for stable isotope analysis, following established preparation methods65 (but see refs. 66,67). The resulting δ13C and δ18O values were measured using a ThermoFisher MAT253+ in six separate measurement blocks per sample at the Earth and Environmental Sciences’ Stable Isotope Geochemistry Laboratory at the University of Queensland. The evolved CO2 gases from the Naxian teeth were analysed for carbon and oxygen isotope compositions using a Thermo Delta V Advantage isotope ratio mass spectrometer housed at the Key Laboratory of Archaeological Sciences and Technology, Shandong University. Stable isotope measurements on the three H. erectus teeth were carried out at the Service de spectrométrie de masse isotopique du Muséum national d’Histoire naturelle, Paris, and analysed using a Thermo Delta V Advantage isotope ratio mass spectrometer. To assess isotopic differences among sites, we applied non-parametric and multivariate tests. For univariate comparisons, Kruskal–Wallis tests revealed highly significant differences in both δ13Ccarbon source (χ² = 181.5, d.f. = 6, P < 0.001) and δ18O (χ² = 114.4, d.f. = 6, P < 0.001) among sites. All statistical analyses were conducted using the open-source program R software (v.4.5.1)68.

Three in situ samples were collected in bulk (CBAX2, CBAX3, CBAX4) from the breccia at Baxian and the clumped isotope analysis was undertaken in the Macquarie GeoAnalytical Stable Isotope Facility using a ThermoFisher dual-inlet MAT253+ mass spectrometer. The results were processed using the Easotope software package69. The final Δ47 value for each sample was then averaged and reported with 95% confidence intervals, before temperatures were calculated using the calibration in ref. 70 for 90 °C reactions. Using these temperatures, the oxygen isotopic composition of the precipitating fluid (δ18Ofluid) was calculated using the equation in ref. 71.

One H. erectus tooth from Baxian was sectioned with a high-precision diamond saw and polished to a smoothness of greater than 5 μm. Laser ablation combined with ICP-MS was used for trace elemental mapping analyses using an ESI NWR193 coupled to an Agilent 7900 ICP-MS at GARG, Southern Cross University, according to the procedures in refs. 19,72. A laser spot size of 40 μm, a scan speed of 80 μm s−¹, a laser intensity of 60% (approximately 1 J mm−2) and a total integration time of 0.50 s were used to produce data points that corresponded to a pixel size of approximately 40 × 40 μm. NIST610 and NIST612 (certified standard reference materials) were used to assess signal drift. Strontium isotope analysis (87Sr/86Sr) was conducted on four H. erectus teeth: one from Baxian cave and three from Naxian cave, also using laser-ablation MC-ICP-MS at the GARG facility. Enamel fragments were carefully extracted from regions showing low uranium concentrations and distinct elemental signatures from the surrounding dentine according to the mapping results. To contextualize the 87Sr/86Sr values obtained and assess potential mobility patterns, a regional strontium isoscape was constructed for southern China and northern Southeast Asia. The isoscape modelling was based on random forest ensemble machine learning analyses adapted from the original script developed in ref. 33 and followed the method fully described in ref. 21.

a-d Naxian cave, a and b the cave – location marked with a red star - is situated on the outer cone of a karst inselberg located close to a highway. c a montage of images to demonstrate the speleology of the cave with the small entrance and flowstone step that leads into the stalagmite chamber dense with speleothem, a larger chamber with narrow and high ceilings and terminating with a small fossil chamber with breccia, d the fossil bearing breccia at the highest point of the cave capped with flowstone and underlain by a younger underlying mixed material below. e-h Baxian Cave e and f the cave is also situated on the outer edge of a karst cone with the limestone corridor than connects both caves, cave location is marked with a red star, g a montage of images to demonstrate the speleology and sedimentology of the cave from the wide and high entrance to the narrower and smaller passage that lead to the confined fossil chamber, h the fossil bearing breccia at the highest point of the cave capped with flowstone and underlain with the younger underlying mixed material. There is a remarkable similarity between the stratigraphy and sedimentology of these deposits and associated fossils (d, h).

The images of the fossil chambers are taken from a 3D models of the caves (Supplementary Information 2 for links).
